sources.title: Haim Brezis, Functional Analysis, Sobolev Spaces and Partial Differential Equations (2011)
sources.locator: §§1.1–1.2, printed pp.1–8; §1.3 first evaluation/isometry paragraph, pp.8–9. PDF pages 16–24 (one-based).
sources.support: Real extension, norming, gauges, open/compact separation, bidual. Proofs are transplanted only after replacing the Zorn conclusion by the explicit HB hypothesis.

contents.name: Theorem 1.1: real dominated extension
Theorem 1.1 instantiated with named data
Lemma 1.1: Zorn; maximal-extension proof of Theorem 1.1
Dual and its norm
Completeness of the dual
Corollary 1.2: preservation of the norm
Corollaries 1.3–1.4: norming and dual-ball maximum
Remark 2: norming functional need not be unique; duality map
Remark 2: uniqueness under strict convexity of the dual
contents.reason: Uniqueness and nonlinear duality maps are not prerequisites of relative norming or separation; this pair proves existence with no strict-convexity hypothesis.

contents.name: Remark 3: fixed-functional norm attainment, reflexivity, and James criterion
contents.reason: Norm attainment for every fixed functional is a reflexivity issue; it must not be confused with norming each fixed vector here.

contents.name: Affine hyperplanes and definitions of separation
Proposition 1.5: closed hyperplanes and continuous functionals
Lemma 1.2: gauge definition and properties
Lemma 1.2: sublinearity, linear upper bound, open strict sublevel set
Lemma 1.3: separating an open convex set from a point
Theorem 1.6: disjoint convex sets, one open
Theorem 1.7: compact versus closed convex sets
Closed-minus-compact step in Theorem 1.7
Remark 4: separation without openness; finite-dimensional exception
contents.reason: These hypothesis-sharpness examples and finite-dimensional separation belong to the existing geometric separation companion; no stronger claim is made here.

contents.name: Corollary 1.8 and Remark 5: detecting closure and density by functionals
Bidual and canonical evaluation construction
contents.locator: §1.3, pp.8–9 through the first isometry formula

contents.name: Isometry of the evaluation embedding
contents.locator: §1.3, pp.8–9 through the first isometry formula

sources.locator: Theorem 4.13 through the complete proof of Theorem 4.20, printed pp.112–116; complete §5.1, pp.137–141 including Problems 5.1–5.4.
sources.support: Independent complex realification and phase argument; gauge proof and geometric separation. The exact version and errors are recorded in notes.

contents.name: Theorem 4.13: real convex-majorant extension, used for sublinear majorants
Lower bound from evaluation at the negative vector
Theorem 4.14: complexification from the real part
Corollary 4.15: norm-preserving extension
Corollary 4.16: a total family detects the zero vector
Example: extending the limit from convergent sequences to ell-infinity
contents.reason: Generalized limits and the failure of an ell-one representation are a different application already assigned to the analytic Hahn–Banach companion.

contents.name: Corollary 4.17: subspace distance attained by a norm-one annihilating functional
Corollary 4.18: annihilating functionals detect subspace closure
Corollary 4.19: finite biorthogonal families modulo a closed subspace
contents.reason: This finite interpolation result is not needed by the pointwise norming or gauge proof. Its natural consumer is finite-dimensional complementation on the geometric separation page.

contents.name: Theorem 4.20: canonical embedding into the bidual
contents.locator: pp.115–116, through the complete theorem proof

contents.name: Upper estimate in Theorem 4.20
Gauge, absorption, and examples of balls, strips, and nonabsorbing sets
Topological vector space and continuous-dual conventions
contents.reason: General topological vector spaces require the separately planned locally convex supplier. This pair deliberately uses the normed-space special case specified by the design.

contents.name: Lemma 5.1: positive homogeneity, subadditivity, sublevel sets
Theorem 5.2: real geometric Hahn–Banach
Theorem 5.3: complex geometric Hahn–Banach
Example: c0 finite sequences with positive last nonzero coordinate
contents.reason: This sharpness example belongs to the geometric separation companion. The relative theorem retains the open-set hypothesis and makes no unsupported separation claim.

contents.name: Corollary 5.4: compact versus closed separation in a locally convex space
Finite-cover construction in Corollary 5.4
Absolute convexity observation (5.7)
contents.reason: Two nonempty absolutely convex sets both contain zero, so they cannot satisfy the disjointness hypotheses here. This vacuous specialization supplies no proof step.

contents.name: Corollary 5.5: locally convex subspace separation
contents.reason: The normed-space consequences are already on the geometric page; arbitrary locally convex domains require the later general-topology interface.

contents.name: Corollary 5.6: continuous extension from locally convex subspaces
contents.reason: Continuity without one norm as majorant is the later locally convex extension problem, outside this normed-space pair.

contents.name: Problem 5.1: a sum is open when one summand is open
Problem 5.2: failure of uniform strict separation without compactness
contents.reason: The geometric separation companion owns the examples showing why two merely closed convex sets need not have a positive separation gap.

contents.name: Problems 5.3–5.4: polar calculus and bipolar theorem
contents.reason: Polar closure needs the locally convex and weak-topology development; none of those results is needed for the relative gauge proof.
